title_en: Notice of the Supreme People's Court, the Supreme People's Procuratorate, the Ministry of Public Security, the Ministry of State Security, and the Ministry of Justice on Issuing the Regulations on Several Issues Concerning the Review and Judgment of Evidence in Death Penalty Cases and the Regulations on Several Issues Concerning the Exclusion of Illegally Obtained Evidence in Criminal Cases
keywords_en: Regarding the handling of death penalty cases; Regarding the handling of criminal cases
full_text_en:
Supreme People's Court Supreme People's Procuratorate

Ministry of Public Security Ministry of State Security Ministry of Justice

Notice on Issuing the "Provisions on Several Issues Concerning the Examination and Judgment of Evidence in Death Penalty Cases" and the "Provisions on Several Issues Concerning the Exclusion of Illegal Evidence in Criminal Cases"

Fa Fa [2010] No. 20

To the Higher People's Courts, People's Procuratorates, Public Security Departments (Bureaus), State Security Departments (Bureaus), and Justice Departments (Bureaus) of all provinces, autonomous regions, and municipalities directly under the Central Government; the Military Court of the People's Liberation Army, the Military Procuratorate of the People's Liberation Army, and the Political Department Security Department of the General Political Department; the Production and Construction Corps Branch of the Higher People's Court of the Xinjiang Uygur Autonomous Region, the People's Procuratorate of the Xinjiang Production and Construction Corps, the Public Security Bureau, the Justice Bureau, and the Prison Administration Bureau:

In order to further improve China's criminal procedure system, in accordance with the central government's overall plan for deepening the reform of the judicial system and working mechanisms, and after extensive and in-depth investigation and research, the Supreme People's Court, the Supreme People's Procuratorate, the Ministry of Public Security, the Ministry of State Security, and the Ministry of Justice have jointly formulated the "Provisions on Several Issues Concerning the Examination and Judgment of Evidence in Death Penalty Cases" and the "Provisions on Several Issues Concerning the Exclusion of Illegal Evidence in Criminal Cases" (hereinafter referred to as the two "Provisions"), which are hereby issued to you for strict compliance.

In order to strictly implement and enforce the two Provisions in judicial practice, the following opinions are put forward:

I. Fully Understand the Significance of Formulating and Implementing the Two Provisions

The two Provisions impose higher standards and stricter requirements on political and legal organs in handling criminal cases, especially death penalty cases. They are of great significance for improving China's criminal procedure system, raising the level of law enforcement and case handling, and promoting the construction of socialist rule of law. Relevant departments of all provinces, autonomous regions, and municipalities directly under the Central Government shall, from the perspective of comprehensively and accurately implementing national laws and carrying out the Party's and the state's criminal policies, actively strengthen publicity work and fully understand the significance of the introduction of the two Provisions.

II. Organize and Carry Out Training on the Two Provisions in a Serious Manner

People's courts, people's procuratorates, public security organs, state security organs, and judicial administrative units and departments at all levels shall, according to actual circumstances, through different channels and in different ways, seriously and promptly carry out training and study work on the two Provisions. They shall carefully organize relevant case-handling personnel to participate in specialized training to ensure that every criminal case-handling personnel can fully master the specific contents of the two Provisions.

III. Strictly Implement and Enforce the Two Provisions

The two Provisions not only comprehensively stipulate the basic principles of evidence in criminal proceedings and refine the standard of proof, but also further specify the collection, fixation, examination, judgment, and use of various types of evidence; they not only define the connotation and extension of illegal evidence, but also specifically regulate the procedures for examining and excluding illegal evidence, the burden of proof, and other issues. Ensuring the proper implementation and enforcement of the two Provisions will play an important role in further improving the level of law enforcement and case handling and further strengthening the quality of law enforcement personnel. All relevant departments shall strictly implement the two Provisions in judicial practice, firmly establish the concept of equal emphasis on punishing crime and protecting human rights, and the concept of equal emphasis on substantive law and procedural law, collect, examine, and judge evidence lawfully, comprehensively, and objectively, strictly control the facts and evidence, effectively improve the quality of criminal case trials, ensure that the two Provisions are implemented, and handle every criminal case as an irrefutable case. New situations, new problems encountered during implementation, and new experiences and new practices discovered shall be carefully summarized and promptly reported to the central competent departments.

In addition, when handling other criminal cases, reference shall be made to the "Provisions on Several Issues Concerning the Examination and Judgment of Evidence in Death Penalty Cases."

June 13, 2010

Provisions on Several Issues Concerning the Examination and Judgment of Evidence in Death Penalty Cases

In order to handle death penalty cases lawfully, fairly, accurately, and prudently, punish crime, and protect human rights, these Provisions are formulated in accordance with the "Criminal Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China" and other relevant legal provisions, combined with judicial practice.

I. General Provisions

Article 1 When handling death penalty cases, the Criminal Law and the Criminal Procedure Law must be strictly implemented, so as to truly achieve clear facts, reliable and sufficient evidence, lawful procedures, correct application of law, and ensure the quality of the case.

Article 2 Determination of the facts of a case must be based on evidence.

Article 3 Investigators, procurators, and judges shall strictly comply with legal procedures and collect, examine, verify, and determine evidence comprehensively and objectively.

Article 4 Only evidence that has been verified through court proceedings such as presentation in court, identification, and cross-examination may serve as the basis for conviction and sentencing.

Article 5 When handling a death penalty case, the determination of the defendant's criminal facts must reach the standard of reliable and sufficient evidence.

Reliable and sufficient evidence means:

(1) The facts of conviction and sentencing are all supported by evidence;

(2) Each piece of evidence used to determine the case has been verified to be true through legal procedures;

(3) There is no contradiction between pieces of evidence, or between evidence and the facts of the case, or any contradiction has been reasonably eliminated;

(4) In joint crime cases, the status and role of the defendant have been clarified;

(5) The process of determining the facts of the case based on evidence conforms to logical and experiential rules, and the conclusion drawn from the evidence is the only conclusion.

When handling a death penalty case, the proof of the following facts must reach the standard of reliable and sufficient evidence:

(1) The occurrence of the alleged criminal fact;

(2) That the defendant committed the criminal act, and the time, place, means, consequences, and other circumstances of the defendant's commission of the criminal act;

(3) The identity status affecting the defendant's conviction;

(4) The defendant has criminal responsibility capacity;

(5) The defendant's culpability;

(6) Whether it is a joint crime and the defendant's status and role in the joint crime;

(7) Facts that warrant a heavier punishment for the defendant.

II. Classified Examination and Determination of Evidence

1. Physical Evidence and Documentary Evidence

Article 6 The following contents shall be focused on when examining physical evidence and documentary evidence:

(1) Whether the physical evidence or documentary evidence is the original item or original document; whether photographs, videos, or reproductions of physical evidence, and copies or reproductions of documentary evidence, match the original item or original document; whether the physical evidence or documentary evidence has been identified or appraised; whether the photographs, videos, or reproductions of physical evidence, and copies or reproductions of documentary evidence, were made by at least two persons, and whether there is a written description and signature from the maker regarding the production process and the location of the original document or item.

(2) Whether the procedures and methods of collecting physical evidence and documentary evidence comply with the law and relevant provisions; whether physical evidence and documentary evidence obtained through inquest, inspection, search, seizure, or impoundment are accompanied by relevant records or lists; whether the records or lists are signed by investigators, the holder of the item, and witnesses; if the holder of the item has not signed, whether the reason is noted; whether the characteristics, quantity, quality, name, etc., of the item are clearly stated.

(3) Whether the physical evidence or documentary evidence was damaged or altered during collection, storage, or appraisal.

(4) Whether the physical evidence or documentary evidence is related to the facts of the case. Whether biological evidence, traces, or items left at the scene related to the crime that are suitable for inspection and appraisal, such as bloodstains, fingerprints, hair, and bodily fluids, have been subjected to DNA identification, fingerprint identification, or other identification methods to make a same-identity determination with the corresponding biological samples, biological characteristics, or items of the defendant or the victim.

(5) Whether all physical evidence and documentary evidence related to the facts of the case have been comprehensively collected.

Article 7 If traces or items that may be related to the facts of the case, such as bloodstains, fingerprints, footprints, handwriting, hair, bodily fluids, or human tissues, discovered during inquest, inspection, or search, should have been collected but were not, or should have been tested but were not, resulting in doubts about the facts of the case, the people's court shall explain the situation to the people's procuratorate. The people's procuratorate may, according to law, supplement the collection or obtain evidence, make a reasonable explanation, or return the case to the investigative organ for supplementary investigation to obtain the relevant evidence.

Article 8 Physical evidence used to determine a case shall be the original item. Only when it is inconvenient to transport the original item, it is not easy to preserve, or it should be kept or disposed of by the relevant department according to law, or it should be returned according to law, may photographs, videos, or reproductions be taken or made that sufficiently reflect the appearance or content of the original item. Photographs, videos, or reproductions of physical evidence may be used as the basis for determining the case if they have been verified to be consistent with the original item, proven to be authentic through appraisal, or otherwise reliably proven to be authentic. If the photographs, videos, or reproductions of the original item cannot reflect the appearance and characteristics of the original item, they cannot be used as the basis for determining the case.

Documentary evidence used to determine a case shall be the original document. Only when it is genuinely difficult to obtain the original document may copies or reproductions be used. Copies or reproductions of documentary evidence may be used as the basis for determining the case if they have been verified to be consistent with the original document, proven to be authentic through appraisal, or otherwise reliably proven to be authentic. If the documentary evidence has alterations or signs of alteration that cannot be reasonably explained, or if the copies or reproductions of the documentary evidence cannot reflect the original document and its content, they cannot be used as the basis for determining the case.

Article 9 If physical evidence or documentary evidence obtained through inquest, inspection, search, seizure, or impoundment is not accompanied by an inquest or inspection record, a search record, a seizure record, or a list of impounded items, and the source of the physical evidence or documentary evidence cannot be proven, it cannot be used as the basis for determining the case.

If the procedures and methods of collecting physical evidence or documentary evidence have the following defects, they may be adopted after correction or reasonable explanation by the relevant case-handling personnel:

(1) The collected or obtained physical evidence or documentary evidence lacks signatures from investigators, the holder of the item, or witnesses on the inquest or inspection record, search record, seizure record, or list of impounded items, or the characteristics, quantity, quality, name, etc., of the item are not clearly stated;

(2) The collected or obtained photographs, videos, or reproductions of physical evidence, or copies or reproductions of documentary evidence, do not note that they have been verified to be consistent with the original, lack the time of reproduction, or lack the signature (seal) of the person or unit that collected or obtained them;

(3) The photographs, videos, or reproductions of physical evidence, or copies or reproductions of documentary evidence, lack a description from the maker regarding the production process and the location of the original item or document, or the description lacks a signature;

(4) Other defects exist in the procedures and methods of collecting physical evidence or documentary evidence.

If there are doubts about the source or collection process of physical evidence or documentary evidence that cannot be reasonably explained, such physical evidence or documentary evidence cannot be used as the basis for determining the case.

Article 10 Physical evidence and documentary evidence that meet the conditions for identification shall be submitted to the parties or witnesses for identification, and if necessary, appraisal shall be conducted.

2. Witness Testimony

Article 11 The following contents shall be focused on when examining witness testimony:

(1) Whether the content of the testimony was directly perceived by the witness.

(2) The witness's age, cognitive level, memory ability, and expressive ability at the time of testifying, and whether their physiological or mental state affects their testimony.

(3) Whether the witness has an interest in the parties to the case or the outcome of the case.

(4) Whether the procedures and methods of obtaining the testimony comply with the law and relevant provisions: whether there was any use of violence, threats, inducement, deception, or other illegal means to obtain testimony; whether the rule of questioning witnesses individually was violated; whether the record was reviewed and confirmed by the witness and signed (sealed) or fingerprinted; when questioning a minor witness, whether their legal representative was notified to be present and was actually present.

(5) Whether the witness testimony is mutually corroborative with other evidence and whether there are contradictions.

Article 12 Witness testimony obtained by illegal means such as violence or threats cannot be used as the basis for determining the case.

Testimony provided by a witness who is in a state of obvious intoxication, narcotic poisoning, or anesthesia from psychotropic drugs, such that they cannot express themselves correctly, cannot be used as the basis for determining the case.

Conjectural, evaluative, or inferential testimony from a witness cannot be used as evidence, except where it is consistent with facts as judged by general life experience.

Article 13 Witness testimony in any of the following circumstances cannot be used as the basis for determining the case:

(1) Testimony obtained without individually questioning the witness;

(2) Written testimony that has not been reviewed and confirmed by the witness and signed (sealed) or fingerprinted;

(3) When questioning a deaf-mute person, a member of a minority nationality who does not understand the local commonly used language or script, or a foreigner, and a translator should have been provided but was not.

Article 14 If the procedures and methods of collecting witness testimony have the following defects, they may be adopted after correction or reasonable explanation by the relevant case-handling personnel:

(1) The names of the questioner, recorder, or legal representative, or the start and end times or location of the questioning, are not filled in;

(2) The location for questioning the witness does not comply with regulations;

(3) The questioning record does not include a statement informing the witness of the obligation to provide truthful testimony and that intentionally giving false testimony or concealing criminal evidence shall incur legal liability;

(4) The questioning record reflects that the same questioner questioned different witnesses within the same time period.

Article 15 A witness in any of the following circumstances shall be notified by the people's court to appear in court to testify; if the witness does not appear in court after being notified according to law, and their written testimony cannot be confirmed after cross-examination, it cannot be used as the basis for determining the case:

(1) The people's procuratorate, the defendant, or the defendant's defender objects to the witness testimony, and the witness testimony has a significant impact on conviction and sentencing;

(2) The people's court deems that the witness should otherwise appear in court to testify.

If the witness's testimony in court contradicts their pre-trial testimony, and the witness can reasonably explain their change of testimony in court and there is supporting evidence, the in-court testimony shall be adopted.

For the written testimony of a witness who does not appear in court to testify, the opinions of the appearing procurator, the defendant, and the defendant's defender shall be heard, and a comprehensive judgment shall be made in conjunction with other evidence. If there are contradictions in the written testimony of a witness who does not appear in court to testify, and the contradictions cannot be resolved and there is no supporting evidence, it cannot be used as the basis for determining the case.

Article 16 When testifying, a witness shall keep confidential any matters involving state secrets or personal privacy.

Where necessary, the people's court may take protective measures such as restricting public disclosure of the witness's information, restricting questioning, concealing the witness's appearance, or altering the witness's voice when the witness appears in court to testify.

3. Victim Statements

Article 17 The examination and determination of victim statements shall apply the relevant provisions on witness testimony mentioned above.

4. Defendant's Confessions and Defenses

Article 18 The following contents shall be focused on when examining the defendant's confessions and defenses:

(1) Whether the time, place, and identity of the interrogator of the interrogation comply with the law and relevant provisions; whether there are at least two investigators interrogating the defendant; whether the defendant is interrogated individually, etc.

(2) Whether the production and modification of the interrogation record comply with the law and relevant provisions; whether the interrogation record indicates the start and end times and location of the interrogation; whether the defendant is informed of their procedural rights such as the right to apply for recusal and the right to retain a lawyer during the first interrogation; whether the defendant has reviewed and confirmed the record and signed (sealed) or fingerprinted it; whether at least two interrogators have signed, etc.

(3) When interrogating a deaf-mute person, a member of a minority nationality, or a foreigner, whether a person proficient in sign language or an interpreter was provided; when interrogating a minor co-defendant, whether their legal representative was notified to be present and was actually present.

(4) Whether the defendant's confession was obtained by illegal means such as extorting a confession by torture; where necessary, the defendant's health examination records and records upon entering and leaving the detention center may be obtained.

(5) Whether the defendant's confessions are consistent before and after, whether there are any reversals, and the reasons for any reversals; whether all of the defendant's confessions and defenses have been collected and placed in the case file; if confessions and defenses that should be in the file are not included, whether a relevant explanation has been provided.

(6) Whether the content of the defendant's defenses is consistent with the facts of the case and common sense, and whether there are contradictions.

(7) Whether the defendant's confessions and defenses are mutually corroborative with the confessions and defenses of co-defendants and other evidence, and whether there are contradictions.

For the above content, if the investigative organ has submitted audio or video recordings along with the case, a review shall be conducted in conjunction with the relevant audio and video recordings.

Article 19 A defendant's confession obtained by illegal means such as extorting a confession by torture cannot be used as the basis for determining the case.

Article 20 A defendant's confession in any of the following circumstances cannot be used as the basis for determining the case:

(1) The interrogation record has not been reviewed and confirmed by the defendant and signed (sealed) or fingerprinted;

(2) When interrogating a deaf-mute person or a person who does not understand the local commonly used language or script, a person proficient in sign language or an interpreter should have been provided but was not.

Article 21 If the interrogation record has the following defects, it may be adopted after correction or reasonable explanation by the relevant case-handling personnel:

(1) The time of interrogation, interrogator, recorder, legal representative, etc., filled in the record are incorrect or contradictory;

(2) The interrogator has not signed;

(3) The record of the first interrogation does not include a statement informing the interrogated person of their procedural rights.

Article 22 The examination of the defendant's confessions and defenses shall be conducted in conjunction with all evidence provided by both the prosecution and the defense, as well as all of the defendant's own confessions and defenses.

If the defendant's pre-trial confessions are consistent, but the defendant reverses them during the trial, and the defendant cannot reasonably explain the reasons for the reversal, or the defendant's defenses contradict all other evidence in the case, but the pre-trial confessions are mutually corroborative with other evidence, the pre-trial confessions may be adopted.

If the defendant's pre-trial confessions and defenses have inconsistencies, but the defendant confesses during the trial, and the in-trial confession is corroborated by other evidence, the in-trial confession may be adopted; if the defendant's pre-trial confessions and defenses have inconsistencies, the defendant does not confess during the trial, and there is no other evidence to corroborate the pre-trial confessions, the pre-trial confessions cannot be adopted.

5. Expert Opinions

Article 23 The following contents shall be focused on when examining expert opinions:

(1) Whether there are circumstances where the expert should have withdrawn but did not.

(2) Whether the expert institution and the expert have lawful qualifications.

(3) Whether the expert procedures comply with the law and relevant provisions.

(4) Whether the source, acquisition, storage, and submission of the sample for examination comply with the law and relevant provisions; whether they are consistent with the contents recorded in the relevant seizure records and lists of impounded items; whether the sample is sufficient and reliable.

(5) Whether the procedures, methods, and analysis process of the expert opinion comply with the inspection and appraisal procedures and technical method requirements of the profession.

(6) Whether the formal elements of the expert opinion are complete; whether it indicates the reason for commissioning the expert opinion, the client, the expert institution, the expert requirements, the expert process, the inspection method, the date of the expert document, and other relevant content; whether it bears the expert institution's special seal and the signature and seal of the expert.

(7) Whether the expert opinion is clear.

(8) Whether the expert opinion is related to the facts to be proven in the case.

(9) Whether there are contradictions between the expert opinion and other evidence, and whether there are contradictions between the expert opinion and the inspection records and related photographs.

(10) Whether the expert opinion has been timely informed to the relevant persons according to law, and whether the parties have objections to the expert opinion.

Article 24 If an expert opinion has any of the following circumstances, it cannot be used as the basis for determining the case:

(1) The expert institution does not have lawful qualifications and conditions, or the expert matter exceeds the scope of projects or capability of the expert institution;

(2) The expert does not possess the statutory qualifications and conditions, does not have the relevant professional skills or titles, or violates the recusal provisions;

(3) There are errors in the expert evaluation procedures or methods;

(4) The expert opinion has no connection with the object of proof;

(5) The subject matter of the expert evaluation is inconsistent with the submitted materials or samples;

(6) The source of the submitted materials or samples is unknown, or they are indeed contaminated and do not meet the conditions for expert evaluation;

(7) Violation of relevant specific standards for expert evaluation;

(8) The expert evaluation document lacks signatures or seals;

(9) Other circumstances that violate relevant provisions.

If there is doubt about an expert opinion, the people's court shall, in accordance with the law, notify the expert to appear in court to testify or provide a relevant explanation, or may supplement the expert evaluation or conduct a new expert evaluation in accordance with the law.

6. Records of Inquests and Inspections

Article 25 The examination of records of inquests and inspections shall focus on the following:

(1) Whether the inquest or inspection was conducted in accordance with the law, whether the preparation of the records complies with the requirements of the law and relevant provisions, and whether the persons conducting the inquest or inspection and the witnesses have signed or sealed them.

(2) Whether the content of the records of inquests or inspections is comprehensive, detailed, accurate, and standardized: whether it accurately records the reasons for initiating the inquest or inspection, the time, place, persons present, scene orientation, surrounding environment, and other circumstances; whether it accurately describes the location, characteristics, and other details of the scene, objects, persons, bodies, etc., and the process of the inquest, inspection, or search; whether the written records are consistent with the physical objects, drawings, video recordings, or photographs; whether the form and method of fixing evidence are scientific and standardized; whether the scene, objects, traces, etc., have been destroyed or forged, and whether it is the original scene; whether physical features, injury conditions, or physiological conditions have been disguised or changed.

(3) If supplementary inquests or inspections are conducted, whether there are contradictions between the circumstances recorded before and after the inquest or inspection, and whether the reason for the renewed inquest or inspection is explained.

(4) Whether the circumstances recorded in the inquest or inspection records can corroborate other evidence such as the defendant's confession, the victim's statement, or expert opinions, and whether there are any contradictions.

Article 26 If the records of an inquest or inspection clearly do not comply with the law and relevant provisions, and no reasonable explanation or clarification can be provided, they cannot be used as evidence.

If the records of an inquest or inspection have circumstances such as the absence of witnesses during the inquest or inspection, the persons conducting the inquest or inspection and the witnesses failing to sign or seal the records, or the persons conducting the inquest or inspection violating the recusal provisions, their authenticity and relevance shall be examined in conjunction with other evidence in the case.

7. Audio-Visual Materials

Article 27 The examination of audio-visual materials shall focus on the following:

(1) Whether the source of the audio-visual materials is lawful, and whether the parties involved were subjected to threats, inducements, or other circumstances violating the law and relevant provisions during the production process;

(2) Whether the identity of the producer or holder, the time, place, and conditions of production, and the method of production are indicated;

(3) Whether they are originals, whether copies have been made, and the number of copies; if the obtained audio-visual materials are copies, whether they are accompanied by an explanation of the reasons for being unable to obtain the original, the production process, and the location of the original, and whether the producer and the original holder of the audio-visual materials have signed or sealed them;

(4) Whether the content and production process are authentic, and whether there have been any forgeries or alterations such as editing, additions, deletions, or modifications;

(5) Whether the content is relevant to the facts of the case.

If there is doubt about the audio-visual materials, an expert evaluation shall be conducted.

For audio-visual materials, their authenticity and relevance shall be examined in conjunction with other evidence in the case.

Article 28 Audio-visual materials falling under any of the following circumstances cannot be used as the basis for deciding a case:

(1) The authenticity of the audio-visual materials cannot be determined after examination or expert evaluation;

(2) There are objections to the time, place, method, etc., of the production and acquisition of the audio-visual materials, and no reasonable explanation or necessary proof can be provided.

8. Other Provisions

Article 29 For electronic evidence such as emails, electronic data interchange (EDI), online chat records, blogs, text messages, electronic signatures, and domain names, the examination shall mainly focus on the following:

(1) Whether the removable storage media such as disks or CDs storing the electronic evidence are submitted together with the printouts;

(2) Whether the time, place, subject, producer, production process, and equipment conditions of the electronic evidence are indicated;

(3) Whether the procedures and links such as production, storage, transmission, acquisition, collection, and presentation are lawful, and whether the evidence collector, producer, holder, and witnesses have signed or sealed them;

(4) Whether the content is authentic, and whether there have been any forgeries or alterations such as cutting, splicing, tampering, or additions;

(5) Whether the electronic evidence is relevant to the facts of the case.

If there is doubt about the electronic evidence, an expert evaluation shall be conducted.

For electronic evidence, its authenticity and relevance shall be examined in conjunction with other evidence in the case.

Article 30 If there are any of the following circumstances in the identification procedures organized by the investigative authorities, a strict examination shall be conducted; if their authenticity cannot be determined, the identification results cannot be used as the basis for deciding a case:

(1) The identification was not conducted under the auspices of an investigator;

(2) The identifying person was allowed to see the subject of identification before the identification;

(3) The identification activities of the identifying persons were not conducted individually;

(4) The subjects of identification were not mixed with other objects having similar characteristics, or the quantity of the subjects of identification provided did not comply with the provisions; except for specific subjects such as corpses or places;

(5) Obvious hints or obvious suspicion of indication were given to the identifying person during the identification.

If there are any of the following circumstances, the identification results may be used as evidence after the relevant case-handling personnel make corrections or provide reasonable explanations:

(1) The number of investigators presiding over the identification was fewer than two;

(2) The specific features of the subject of identification were not inquired of the identifying person in detail;

(3) A special and standardized identification record was not made of the process and results of the identification, or the identification record was not signed or sealed by the investigators, identifying persons, or witnesses;

(4) The identification record is too simple, containing only the result without the process;

(5) The case file contains only the identification record, without photos, videos, or other materials of the identified subjects, making it impossible to know the true circumstances of the identification.

Article 31 For materials such as the case-solving process issued by the investigative authorities, it shall be examined whether they bear the signature or seal of the case-handling person or the case-handling authority that issued the explanatory material.

If there is doubt about the case-solving process, or if there is doubt about the basis for determining that the defendant is a major suspect, the investigative authorities shall be requested to provide supplementary explanations.

III. Comprehensive Examination and Application of Evidence

Article 32 The probative force of evidence shall be examined and determined by considering the specific circumstances of the case, including the degree of relevance between each piece of evidence and the facts to be proved, and the connections between the pieces of evidence.

Only evidence that is internally linked, jointly points to the same fact to be proved, and can reasonably eliminate contradictions can be used as the basis for deciding a case.

Article 33 If there is no direct evidence proving that the criminal act was committed by the defendant, but the following conditions are simultaneously met, the defendant may be found guilty:

(1) The indirect evidence used to decide the case has been verified and confirmed to be true;

(2) The indirect evidence used to decide the case mutually corroborates each other, without any irresolvable contradictions or inexplicable doubts;

(3) The indirect evidence used to decide the case forms a complete system of proof;

(4) The conclusion drawn from the case facts determined based on indirect evidence is unique and sufficient to exclude all reasonable doubt;

(5) The reasoning conducted using indirect evidence conforms to logic and empirical judgment.

When deciding a case based on indirect evidence, the imposition of the death penalty shall be treated with particular caution.

Article 34 If physical evidence or documentary evidence of a highly concealed nature is obtained based on the defendant's confession or identification, and such evidence mutually corroborates other evidence proving the occurrence of the criminal act, and the possibility of collusion, extortion of confessions, or inducement of confessions is excluded, a guilty verdict may be rendered.

Article 35 Physical evidence, documentary evidence, and other evidentiary materials collected by investigative authorities using special investigative measures in accordance with relevant provisions, if verified to be true by the court, may be used as the basis for deciding a case.

The court shall not disclose the process and methods of the special investigative measures in accordance with the law.

Article 36 After making a determination of guilt against the defendant, when the people's court determines the sentencing facts concerning the defendant, in addition to examining statutory circumstances, it shall also examine the following circumstances affecting sentencing:

(1) The cause of the case;

(2) Whether the victim was at fault and the degree of such fault, and whether the victim bears responsibility for the escalation of the conflict and the extent of that responsibility;

(3) Whether close relatives of the defendant assisted in arresting the defendant;

(4) The defendant's usual conduct and whether the defendant shows remorse;

(5) The situation regarding compensation in the victim's incidental civil action, and whether the defendant has obtained forgiveness from the victim or the victim's close relatives;

(6) Other circumstances affecting sentencing.

If there are both circumstances for leniency or mitigation of punishment and circumstances for aggravation of punishment, a comprehensive consideration shall be given to the relevant circumstances in accordance with the law.

If it cannot be excluded that the defendant has circumstances for leniency or mitigation of punishment, the imposition of the death penalty shall be treated with particular caution.

Article 37 Evidence falling under the following circumstances shall be used with caution and may be accepted if corroborated by other evidence:

(1) Statements, testimony, and confessions made by victims, witnesses, or defendants who suffer from physical or mental defects, who have some difficulty in understanding or expressing the facts of the case, but have not lost the ability to correctly understand or express themselves;

(2) Testimony favorable to the defendant given by a witness who is related to the defendant or has other close relations, or testimony unfavorable to the defendant given by a witness who is in a conflicting interest with the defendant.

Article 38 If the court has doubts about the evidence, it may inform the appearing prosecutors, the defendant, and the defendant's辩护人 to supplement the evidence or provide explanations; if verification is truly necessary, it may adjourn the trial to investigate and verify the evidence. When conducting an out-of-court investigation, the court may, when necessary, notify the appearing prosecutors and the defendant's辩护人 to be present. If the appearing prosecutors, the defendant's辩护人, or both are absent, the court shall record this in the records.

For evidence supplemented by the people's procuratorate or the defendant's辩护人, and evidence obtained through the court's out-of-court investigation and verification, the court may solicit the opinions of the appearing prosecutors and the defendant's辩护人 outside of court. If the opinions of the two sides are inconsistent and one side requests the people's court to open a court session for investigation, the people's court shall do so.

Article 39 If the defendant or their辩护人 raises facts and reasons concerning voluntary surrender (自首) and the relevant authority has not recognized it, the court shall request the relevant authority to provide evidentiary materials or request relevant persons to testify, and determine whether voluntary surrender is established in conjunction with other evidence.

If the evidentiary materials regarding whether and how the defendant assisted in arresting a co-defendant are incomplete, making it impossible to determine that the defendant has performed a meritorious service, the court shall request the relevant authority to provide evidentiary materials or request relevant persons to testify, and determine whether the meritorious service is established in conjunction with other evidence.

If the defendant has reported or disclosed crimes committed by others, it shall be examined whether this has been verified; if it has not yet been verified, verification shall be conducted promptly.

If the evidentiary materials regarding the defendant's status as a repeat offender are incomplete, the relevant authority shall be requested to provide such materials.

Article 40 When examining whether the defendant had reached the age of eighteen at the time of committing the crime, household registration certificates shall generally be used as the basis; if there is an objection to the household registration certificate, and there is verified birth certificate or testimony from disinterested persons proving that the defendant was under eighteen, the defendant shall be deemed to be under eighteen; if there is no household registration certificate and no birth certificate, a comprehensive judgment shall be made based on evidence such as census registration and testimony from disinterested persons, and if necessary, a bone age assessment may be conducted, with the results used as a reference for determining the defendant's age.

If the contradictions between pieces of evidence are not resolved, there is insufficient evidence to prove that the defendant had reached the age of eighteen at the time of committing the alleged crime, and it is truly impossible to ascertain, it shall not be determined that the defendant had reached the age of eighteen.

Article 41 These Provisions shall take effect on July 1, 2010.

Provisions on Several Issues concerning the Exclusion of Illegal Evidence in Criminal Cases

These Provisions are formulated in accordance with the Criminal Procedure Law and relevant judicial interpretations, based on the practical work of the people's courts, people's procuratorates, public security organs, state security organs, and judicial administrative organs in handling criminal cases, in order to standardize judicial conduct and promote judicial fairness.

Article 1 Confessions of a criminal suspect or defendant obtained through illegal means such as extortion of confessions by torture, and witness testimony or victim statements obtained through illegal means such as violence or threats, constitute illegal verbal evidence.

Article 2 Illegal verbal evidence, once confirmed in accordance with the law, shall be excluded and cannot be used as the basis for deciding a case.

Article 3 When reviewing and approving arrests and reviewing for prosecution, the people's procuratorates shall exclude illegal verbal evidence in accordance with the law, and such evidence cannot be used as the basis for approving arrests or initiating public prosecutions.

Article 4 After the copy of the bill of prosecution is served but before the court session begins, if the defendant claims that his pre-trial confession was obtained illegally, he shall submit a written opinion to the people's court. If the defendant has genuine difficulty in writing, he may make an oral statement, and the court personnel or his defense counsel shall make a record, which shall be signed or fingerprinted by the defendant.

The people's court shall submit the defendant's written opinion or a copy of the oral statement record to the people's procuratorate before the court session begins.

Article 5 If the defendant or his defense counsel claims before or during the trial that the defendant's pre-trial confession was obtained illegally, the court shall conduct an immediate investigation during the trial after the prosecutor reads the indictment.

If the defendant or his defense counsel claims before the conclusion of the court debate that the defendant's pre-trial confession was obtained illegally, the court shall also conduct an investigation.

Article 6 If the defendant or his defense counsel claims that the defendant's pre-trial confession was obtained illegally, the court shall request them to provide relevant clues or evidence, such as the identity of the personnel allegedly involved in the illegal evidence collection, the time, place, method, and content.

Article 7 Upon examination, if the court has doubts about the legality of obtaining the defendant's pre-trial confession, the prosecutor shall provide the interrogation record, original audio or video recordings of the interrogation process, or other evidence to the court, and request the court to notify other persons present during the interrogation or other witnesses to appear in court to testify. If the suspicion of extortion of confession by torture still cannot be eliminated, the prosecutor shall request the court to notify the interrogating personnel to appear in court to testify to prove the legality of obtaining the confession. If the prosecutor cannot present evidence during the trial, he may, in accordance with Article 165 of the Criminal Procedure Law, suggest that the court adjourn the trial.

Upon being lawfully notified, the interrogating personnel or other persons shall appear in court to testify.

Explanatory materials submitted by the prosecutor bearing an official seal but not signed or sealed by the relevant interrogating personnel cannot be used as evidence to prove the legality of the evidence collection.

The prosecution and the defense may cross-examine and debate the issue of the legality of obtaining the defendant's pre-trial confession.

Article 8 If the court has doubts about the evidence provided by either the prosecution or the defense, it may adjourn the trial to investigate and verify the evidence. When necessary, it may notify the prosecutors and the defendant's defense counsel to be present.

Article 9 If, during the trial, the prosecutor needs to supplement the investigation to provide new evidence and suggests an adjournment of the trial, the court shall grant it.

If the defendant or his defense counsel requests the court to notify the interrogating personnel, other persons present during the interrogation, or other witnesses to appear in court, and the court deems it necessary, it may adjourn the trial.

Article 10 Upon the court's examination, if any of the following circumstances exist, the defendant's pre-trial confession may be read aloud and cross-examined during the trial:

(1) The defendant or his defense counsel has not provided relevant clues or evidence concerning illegal evidence collection;

(2) The defendant or his defense counsel has provided relevant clues or evidence concerning illegal evidence collection, but the court has no doubt about the legality of obtaining the defendant's pre-trial confession;

(3) The evidence provided by the prosecutor is reliable and sufficient to exclude that the defendant's pre-trial confession was obtained illegally.

For the defendant's pre-trial confession read aloud in court, it shall be determined whether it can be used as the basis for deciding a case in conjunction with the defendant's in-court confession and other evidence.

Article 11 If the prosecutor does not provide evidence to prove the legality of the defendant's pre-trial confession, or the provided evidence is insufficiently reliable or sufficient, that confession cannot be used as the basis for deciding a case.

Article 12 If the court of first instance did not examine the claim raised by the defendant or his defense counsel that the defendant's pre-trial confession was obtained illegally, and used the defendant's pre-trial confession as the basis for deciding the case, the court of second instance shall examine the legality of obtaining the defendant's pre-trial confession. If the prosecutor does not provide evidence to prove it, or the provided evidence is insufficiently reliable or sufficient, that confession of the defendant cannot be used as the basis for deciding a case.

Article 13 If, during the trial, the prosecutor, the defendant, or his defense counsel claims that the written testimony of a witness who did not appear in court or the written statement of a victim who did not appear in court was obtained illegally, the party presenting the evidence shall prove the legality of the evidence collection.

The court shall investigate the evidence referred to in the preceding paragraph by reference to the relevant provisions of these Provisions.

Article 14 If the collection of physical evidence or documentary evidence clearly violates legal provisions and may affect the fairness of the trial, corrections shall be made or reasonable explanations shall be provided; otherwise, that physical evidence or documentary evidence cannot be used as the basis for deciding a case.

Article 15 These Provisions shall take effect on July 1, 2010.
